title: v10.11.7 and ffprobe ram usage
body:
Since I have to systematically recreate my libraries from scratch, as mentioned in https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/issues/15518, I've realized with the release of version 10.11.7 that I can no longer even rescan all the movies in the folder.

I investigated and eventually realized that 8GB of memory on the server is no longer sufficient to scan a 4TB disk of movies.
So I run a 'refresh' of the library and monitor what's happening in a window using the 'htop' command. I see the memory usage gradually increase, reaching 100% RAM usage, then the swap space consumption increases, but it's only 1GB, so it's saturated in 3 seconds. Then the system seems to freeze, or at least very slow, and then Jellyfin restarts on its own.

The server is a VM, so I allocated 16GB, but it made no difference. I also allocated 24GB, and it's the same.

However, there's a setting in the parameters where you can adjust the number of threads. I hadn't configured anything, so I set both fields to 2. With this, I only see two simultaneous ffprobe processes, and RAM consumption reaches about 15GB before dropping, then rising again, and so on.

A least there are no more crashes, so it's still usable. I haven't tried to determine if it actually takes significantly longer than before.

In any case, with version 10.11.6, 8GB was sufficient on the VM.

There's a regression somewhere.

So i let Claude Code analyze and test a bit, and i think it found teh answere or at least part of the problem. I also let it test it and confirming the findings and hope that helps the devs to get this fixxed. Hopefully i dont make someone mad with it, i tryed everything to really test the issue so it doenst halluzinate some bs. 

Im running in a kubernetes cluster on debian vms on proxmox with semver pinned versions on two diffrent Intel ipgu enabled CPUs, but the validation done isnt with enabled hardware rendering so i think it doesnt matter. 

## Root Cause: jellyfin-ffmpeg regression in `-show_frames -only_first_vframe` with Dolby Vision HEVC

The ffprobe binary shipped in the 10.11.7 Docker image has a regression in its Dolby Vision RPU metadata decoder. When decoding the first video frame of a DV HEVC file, memory grows unbounded (~400MB/s) until OOM.

The ffprobe binary from the 10.11.6 Docker image handles the identical file in 3MB.

### Reproduction

Run against any Dolby Vision HEVC Remux file (tested with multiple DV HDR10 files, 30-60GB range):

```bash
# OOM — 10.11.7 ffprobe, ~7.8GB RSS before killed
docker run --rm -v /path/to/media:/media:ro --entrypoint /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe \
  jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.7 \
  -i "file:/media/some_dv_hevc_file.mkv" \
  -threads 0 -v warning -print_format json \
  -show_streams -show_chapters -show_format \
  -show_frames -only_first_vframe

# OK — 10.11.6 ffprobe, 3MB RSS, completes instantly
docker run --rm -v /path/to/media:/media:ro --entrypoint /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe \
  jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.6 \
  -i "file:/media/some_dv_hevc_file.mkv" \
  -threads 0 -v warning -print_format json \
  -show_streams -show_chapters -show_format \
  -show_frames -only_first_vframe

# OK — 10.11.7 ffprobe WITHOUT -show_frames, 5MB RSS
docker run --rm -v /path/to/media:/media:ro --entrypoint /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe \
  jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.7 \
  -i "file:/media/some_dv_hevc_file.mkv" \
  -threads 0 -v warning -print_format json \
  -show_streams -show_chapters -show_format
```

### Binary comparison

Both report `ffprobe version 7.1.3-Jellyfin` but are different builds:

```
10.11.6: e3577e04afc2387157f47952c8f4cc77  /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe
10.11.7: 668ee1bd7934dfe02c7a6c550e2564ef  /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe
```

### Why Jellyfin triggers this

`MediaEncoder.GetMediaInfoInternal()` adds `-show_frames -only_first_vframe` to every video ffprobe call during library scans:

```csharp
// MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Encoder/MediaEncoder.cs line 514
if (protocol == MediaProtocol.File && !isAudio && _proberSupportsFirstVideoFrame)
{
    args += " -show_frames -only_first_vframe";
}
```

When the library scan reaches any DV HEVC file, the ffprobe child process spirals to 7.8GB+ and gets OOM-killed, taking the container with it. This creates an infinite crash loop since the scan always hits the same file after restart.

### Memory trace during OOM

Captured from cgroup + `/proc/PID/status` inside the container (8Gi limit):

```
TIME       .NET process   ffprobe process   Container total
baseline   ~540 MB        —                 542 MB
+10s       567 MB         1,474 MB          1,924 MB
+18s       561 MB         3,543 MB          6,532 MB
+25s       559 MB         5,522 MB          8,190 MB
+32s       557 MB         7,797 MB          8,191 MB → OOM
```

The .NET process stays flat. The OOM is entirely the ffprobe child process.

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
## Confirming and sharing a workaround

I can confirm this on 10.11.7 with jellyfin-ffmpeg7 7.1.3-4 in an LXC container on Proxmox (community script install, not Docker). The bail-out fix from PR #673 is present but doesn't prevent the memory spike, consistent with what @participant9 reported.

My trigger files aren't Dolby Vision. They're standard Bluray 1080p MKV rips (h264) and a WEBDL 1080p, so the issue isn't limited to DV HEVC. The common factor is `-show_frames -only_first_vframe -threads 0` on files where the MKV demuxer has to buffer a large number of interleaved packets before finding the first decodable video frame.

Confirming @participant1's `-threads 0` finding: the issue does not reproduce from the CLI, even with the `file:` protocol prefix and the same flags. It only triggers when Jellyfin invokes ffprobe, which adds `-threads 0` automatically.

### Behavioral details

These may help others choose a workaround:

- `ulimit -v` (virtual memory cap) alone does not kill ffprobe. libavformat's MKV demuxer handles allocation failures gracefully and keeps churning within the capped memory for 60-90+ seconds until the upstream packet-count bail-out finally triggers. Exit code is normal (<=128), not a signal.
- Because of this, a memory cap by itself just means you have a process pinned at the cap, burning CPU for over a minute per affected file, per concurrent scan thread.
- Adding `timeout` is what actually cleans things up promptly.
- Normal ffprobe completes in well under a second and peaks around 30-50 MB RSS, so there's a wide gap between normal and affected behavior.

### Workaround: ffprobe wrapper with dpkg-divert

This replaces ffprobe with a small wrapper that applies a 512 MB virtual memory cap and a 30-second kill timeout. Normal files are completely unaffected. Affected files get killed after 30 seconds, Jellyfin falls back to TMDb/TVDB metadata, and playback works fine.

The `dpkg-divert` makes it upgrade-safe: when `jellyfin-ffmpeg7` gets a package update, the new binary installs to `ffprobe.real` and the wrapper stays in place.

**Step 1: Divert the real binary**

```bash
dpkg-divert --local --rename \
  --divert /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe.real \
  --add /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe
```

**Step 2: Create the wrapper**

Write this to `/usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# ffprobe wrapper: memory cap + timeout to prevent OOM on affected files.
# Normal ffprobe peaks ~30-50 MB. Affected files grow unbounded.
# The 512 MB cap stops growth early; the 30s timeout kills processes
# that churn at the cap without finishing.

VLIMIT_KB=524288   # 512 MB virtual address space
TIMEOUT_SEC=30
REAL=/usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe.real

ulimit -v $VLIMIT_KB
timeout --signal=KILL "$TIMEOUT_SEC" "$REAL" "$@"
rc=$?

# 137 = SIGKILL from timeout; 124 = timeout expired (GNU coreutils)
if [[ $rc -eq 137 || $rc -eq 124 ]]; then
    logger -t ffprobe-oom "rc=${rc} vlimit=${VLIMIT_KB}KB timeout=${TIMEOUT_SEC}s -- $*"
fi
exit $rc
```

Then make it executable:

```bash
chmod 755 /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe
```

**Step 3: Restart Jellyfin**

```bash
systemctl restart jellyfin
```

**Step 4: Check for kills after a library scan**

```bash
journalctl -t ffprobe-oom --no-pager
```

### Reversal

To remove the wrapper and go back to the stock binary:

```bash
rm /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe
dpkg-divert --local --rename --remove /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe
```

### Notes

- For Docker users, you'd need to mount the wrapper into the container or add it in a custom image layer. The `dpkg-divert` approach is for bare-metal and LXC installs where the package manager owns the binary directly.
- I've been running this through full library scans (movies and TV, ~4 TB) on a 4 GB container with default concurrency settings and it's stable. Two affected files get caught and killed every scan, everything else completes normally.

AI helped me write this. Otherwise I would have been too lazy to compile my findings.

comments.body:
I *think* I found the core cause and confirmed with my received samples (not a lot though, only 2).

It is not Dolby Vision related. It is due the mkv having multiple video streams, and some of the video stream is a still image like thumbnail or cover image. And ffprobe's image decoder will behave strangely with auto threading enabled.

See https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-ffmpeg/pull/681 for more info if you are interested.

comments.author: participant21
comments.body:
If anybody is looking to unbreak their jellyfin install because of this bug - I ended up using systemd support for cgroups to limit resource usage. With a 3GB soft memory limit imposed, ffprobe is now prevented from crashing the system.

I personally run jellyfin via flatpak, which automatically creates a cgroup scope that can have resource limits imposed upon it. If you run jellyfin from a systemd service file, it will also be placed within its own scope. 

If you're running jellyfin flatpak, you can add limits to its scope like by creating a directory and a conf file.

$ mkdir ~/.config/systemd/user/app-flatpak-org.jellyfin.JellyfinServer-.scope.d
$ touch ~/.config/systemd/user/app-flatpak-org.jellyfin.JellyfinServer-.scope.d/memlimit.conf

Add the following to memlimit.conf:

```
[Scope]
# Soft memory limit (system start aggressive reclamation
MemoryHigh=3G
# Hard memory limit (killed by OOM)
MemoryMax=4G
# Disable swap
MemorySwapMax=0
```

If you dont use flatpak but you start jellyfin via systemd service file, you can add the above to it (minus the scope heading) to impose memory limits. Hope this can be of some help to folks finding themselves with a broken jellyfin install.

comments.body: Here is a quick workaround for people on debian 13 until the official hotfix version is released: `apt install jellyfin-ffmpeg7=7.1.3-1-trixie` This allows to downgrade ffmpeg to the version used with 10.11.5 while still using jellyfin 10.11.7 so no security issues. When the hotfix is released do an apt full-upgrade to update jellyfin-ffmpeg7 to latest. Also just for information with the 7.1.3-1 version of jellyfin-ffmpeg7 the ffprobe command still uses - threads 0 but the issue doesn't happen, and the mkv file i'm using does not contain a png cover file as shown by mkvtoolnix:

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
For people running PVE Community Scripts, you can login to the LXC and then run 

`apt install jellyfin-ffmpeg7=7.1.3-5-noble`

This will install an earlier version of ffmpeg and this version will also run with `-threads 0` but it will not result in OOM errors or freeze your LXC.
